farraa:4-6.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يُفْرَقُ كُلُّ أَمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ﴾.
﴿أَمْراً﴾ is accusative by His saying يفرق, in the sense: every affair is distinguished, a distinguishing (farqan) and a command (amran); and likewise.
His saying: ﴿رَحْمَةً مِّن رَّبِّكَ﴾: that is distinguished as a mercy from your Lord. And it is allowed to put الرحمة in the accusative by مرسلين falling upon it, making the mercy the Prophet himself, Allah bless him.

farraa:7-7.t:
His saying: ﴿رَبِّ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
Al-Aʿmash and his companions put it in the genitive, and the people of Medina put it in the nominative. Al-Ḥasan also put it in the genitive, so that it follows ربك: "your Lord, the Lord of the heavens".
Whoever puts it in the nominative makes it follow His saying: ﴿إنهُ هُوَ السَّميعُ العَلِيمُ﴾; and another also put it in the nominative by resumption (istiʾnāf), as He said: "وما بينهُما الرحمنُ".

farraa:10-11.t:
His saying: ﴿تَأْتِي ٱلسَّمَآءُ بِدُخَانٍ مُّبِينٍ يَغْشَى ٱلنَّاسَ هَـٰذَا عَذَابٌ﴾.
The Prophet, Allah bless him, had prayed against them, saying: "O Allah, make Your tread heavy upon Muḍar; O Allah, [send on them years] like the years of Joseph." So hunger struck them until they ate bones and carrion, and they would see between themselves and the sky [something like] smoke.
His saying: ﴿يَغْشَى ٱلنَّاسَ هَـٰذَا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾.
By it is meant: that is a punishment. And it is said that the people were saying: "This smoke is a punishment."

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّا كَاشِفُو ٱلْعَذَابِ قَلِيلاً إِنَّكُمْ عَآئِدُونَ﴾.
It is said: returning to your shirk; and it is said: returning to the punishment of the Hereafter.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ﴾.
He means: the Day of Badr, and it is the greatest assault.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿رَسُولٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾.
I.e. honoured with his Lord; and it may be "noble among his people", because he said: no prophet was sent except that he was of the noblest of his people.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿أَنْ أَدُّوۤاْ إِلَيَّ عِبَادَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
He says: hand them over to me, send them with me; and that is His saying: ﴿أَرْسِلْ مَعِىَ بَنىِ إِسْرَائيلَ﴾.
And it is said: "Render to me [your obedience], O servants of Allah"; in the first interpretation العباد is accusative by أدوا.

farraa:20-20.t:
His saying: ﴿أَن تَرْجُمُونِ﴾.
Al-rajm (stoning) here is killing.

farraa:21-21.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِن لَّمْ تُؤْمِنُواْ لِي فَٱعْتَزِلُونِ﴾.
He says: then leave me, neither against me nor for me.

farraa:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿فَدَعَا رَبَّهُ أَنَّ هَـٰؤُلاَءِ قَوْمٌ﴾.
You give (أنَّ) fatḥa; and had you implied a verb of saying and given it kasra, it would have been correct.

farraa:24-24.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱتْرُكِ ٱلْبَحْرَ رَهْواً﴾.
He says: still. He said: and Abū Tharwān recited to me:
كأنما أهلُ حجر ينظرون مَتى * يَرَونَنى خارجاً طير تَنَادِيد طيرٌ رأَتْ بازياً نَضْخُ الدماءِ به * أو أمةٌ خرجَتْ رهواً إلى عيد
(It is as if the people of Ḥajr, watching for when they will see me coming out, are scattering birds: birds that have seen a falcon spattered with blood, or a slave-girl who went out leisurely (rahwan) to a festival.)

farraa:26-29.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَقَامٍ كَرِيمٍ﴾.
It is said: fine dwellings; and it is said: the pulpits.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Abū Shuʿayb narrated to me, from Manṣūr ibn al-Muʿtamir, from al-Minhāl ibn ʿAmr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, regarding His saying: ﴿فَمَا بَكَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلسَّمَآءُ وَٱلأَرْضُ﴾: he said: for the believer, his place of prayer on earth weeps over him, and the place in heaven where his deeds ascend weeps over him.
Al-Farrāʾ said: and so Ḥibbān reported it, from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās.

farraa:30-30.t:
His saying: ﴿مِنَ ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلْمُهِينِ﴾; and in the text (ḥarf) of ʿAbd Allāh: "مِنْ عَذَابِ المُهِين".
This is among what is annexed to itself because the two nouns differ, like His saying: ﴿ولَدَارُ الآخِرَةِ خيرٌ﴾, and like His saying: ﴿وذَلِكَ دِينُ الْقَيِّمَةِ﴾, which in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh is: "وذلك الدينُ القَيِّمَةُ".

farraa:33-33.t:
His saying: ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُم مِّنَ ٱلآيَاتِ مَا فِيهِ بَلاَءٌ مُّبِينٌ﴾.
He means: clear favours, among them that He saved them from the people of Pharaoh, shaded them with clouds, and sent down to them manna and quails. It is as you say to a man: "My favour (balāʾ) towards you is surely good." And it has been said concerning them that al-balāʾ is punishment; and all is correct.

farraa:36-36.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأْتُواْ بِآبَآئِنَا إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾.
They address the Prophet, Allah bless him, alone; and it is like His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها النَّبىُّ إذا طلَّقتُمُ النِّساءَ﴾. In much of the speech of the Arabs, the Arabs put the action of one in the plural; of that is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ أرْجِعونِ﴾.

farraa:39-39.t:
His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ بِٱلْحَقِّ﴾.
He means: for the truth.

farraa:40-40.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ يَوْمَ ٱلْفَصْلِ مِيقَاتُهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾.
He means: the first and the last. Had ﴿مِيقَاتُهم﴾ been put in the accusative, it would have been correct, making "the day" an adverb (ṣifa). He said: one of them recited to me:
لو كنت أعلم أنّ آخر عهدكم * يوم الرحيل فعلت ما لم أفعل
(Had I known that my last meeting with you was on the day of departure, I would have done what I did not do.)
So he put يوم الرحيل in the accusative, as an adverb (ṣifa).
«[Translator's note: ṣifa here is al-Farrāʾ's Kufan term for the adverbial (ẓarf), not "adjective".]»

farraa:42-42.t:
His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ مَن رَّحِمَ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
For the believers intercede for one another. If you wish, make مَن in the position of the nominative, as though you said: "No one stands except so-and-so"; and if you wish, you make it accusative by exception (istithnāʾ), cut off from the beginning of the speech, meaning: "O Allah, except whom You have had mercy upon."

farraa:44-44.t:
His saying: ﴿طَعَامُ ٱلأَثِيمِ﴾.
He means: the wicked.

farraa:45-45.t:
His saying: ﴿كَٱلْمُهْلِ تَغْلِي﴾.
Many of the companions of ʿAbd Allāh read it: "تغلى", and it has been reported from ʿAbd Allāh, and the people of Medina read it likewise; and al-Ḥasan read it "يغلى", making it refer to the food or to the muhl (molten brass). Whoever makes it feminine refers to the feminine of the tree.
Like it is His saying: ﴿أَمَنَةً نُعاساً﴾: تغشى and يغشى; the masculine is for the drowsiness (nuʿās), and the feminine for the security (amana). And like it: ﴿أَلَمْ يَكُ نُطْفَةً مِنْ مَّنِىٍّ تُمْنَى﴾: the feminine is for the nuṭfa (drop), and the masculine from the manī (semen).

farraa:47-47.t:
His saying: ﴿فَٱعْتِلُوهُ﴾.
ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read it with kasra, and the people of Medina read it: "فاعتلُوه", with ḍamma on the tāʾ.

farraa:49-49.t:
His saying: ﴿ذُقْ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْكَرِيمُ﴾.
The readers read it with kasra on the alif. Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: a shaykh narrated to me, from Ḥujr, from Abū Qatāda al-Anṣārī, from his father, who said: I heard al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib say on the pulpit: "ذُقْ أَنك", with fatḥa on the alif. The meaning with fatḥa is: taste, because of this saying which you said in the world. Whoever uses kasra relates his saying. That is because Abū Jahl met the Prophet, Allah bless him; he said: the Prophet, Allah bless him, took hold of him and shook him, then said [to him]: "Woe to you, O Abū Jahl, woe!" And Allah sent it down as the Prophet, Allah bless him, said it. Abū Jahl answered him and said: "[By] Allah, neither you nor your Lord has power over me; I am the most honoured of the people of the valley among his people, and the mightiest of them." So it was revealed as he had said it. He said: so its meaning, as we see it, and Allah knows best, is that it is a rebuke, i.e. [173/b] taste, for you are honoured as you claimed, while you are not so.

farraa:51-51.t:
His saying: ﴿فِي مَقَامٍ أَمِينٍ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim read it: ﴿مَقامٍ﴾, and the people of Medina read it (فى مُقام), with ḍamma on the mīm.
Al-maqām with fatḥa on the mīm is better in Arabic, because it is the place; and al-muqām is the staying; and all is correct.

farraa:54-54.t:
His saying: ﴿وَزَوَّجْنَاهُم بِحُورٍ عِينٍ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "وَأَمْدَدْناهُمْ بِعِيسٍ عِين"; al-ʿaysāʾ is the white one, and al-ḥawrāʾ likewise.

farraa:56-57.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَ يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا ٱلْمَوْتَ إِلاَّ ٱلْمَوْتَةَ ٱلأُولَىٰ﴾.
Someone may say: how did He except a death in the world that has passed from the death of the Hereafter? This is like His saying: ﴿ولا تَنْكِحُوا ما نَكَحَ آباؤُكم من النِّساءِ إِلاَّ ما قَدْ سَلَفَ﴾: إلا in this place is in the position of سوى (other than), as though He said: do not marry, do not do other than what your fathers did. Likewise His saying: ﴿لا يذُوقون فيها الموتَ﴾: other than the first death. And like it: ﴿خالدِينَ فيها ما دَامتِ السّماوَاتُ والأرضُ إِلا مَا شَاءَ ربُّك﴾, i.e. besides what your Lord has willed for them of addition of immortality beyond the measure of the world. And you say in speech: "You have a thousand with me, except (إلا) what you have through so-and-so", and its meaning is: besides what you have with me through so-and-so. So إلا may be a subtraction from what precedes it or an addition to it. What we have mentioned to you of these verses is an addition to what precedes إلا; and subtraction from what precedes إلا is your saying: "These are a thousand except a hundred", the meaning being: they are a thousand less a hundred.
His saying: ﴿وَوَقَاهُمْ عَذَابَ ٱلْجَحِيمِ فضلاً﴾.
I.e. He did it as a favour from Him; and it is among what, had it come in the nominative, would have been correct, i.e.: that is a favour from your Lord.
